exposure: leaving the placenta in situ for subsequent reabsorption of the placenta or delayed hysterectomy
manual removal of placenta during cesarean section
focal resection of the affected uterine wall
termination of pregnancy before the viable gestational age
manual removal of placenta after vaginal delivery
cohort: 442 women with PAS from 15 referral centers of the International Society of PAS (IS-PAS)
finding: In referral centers, the most common management for severe PAS was cesarean hysterectomy, followed by leaving the placenta in situ and focal resection.
mod_finding: Cesarean hysterectomy was the most common mode of delivery in women with severe PAS, followed by leaving the placenta in situ and focal resection.
